2609.17225.title: Psychological Effects of Cultural Upheavals from Millions of Song Lyrics Over 100 Years
2609.17225.paper_summary: Cultural upheavals impact many aspects of social life, and many studies have investigated their impact on language patterns. However, few investigations have isolated the impact of upheavals on individuals at scale in popular media. The current work evaluated millions of song lyrics spanning more than a century in search of within-artist and between-artist signals of distress from the Vietnam War, the terrorist attacks of 9/11, and COVID-19. Compared to a five-year baseline, rates of self-references - a marker of psychological distancing - were significantly reduced after the Vietnam War and September 11th. Cognitive processing terms were elevated post-upheaval vs. pre-upheaval, which indicated artists' increased attempts to make meaning from such massive disruptions. Content patterns corroborated these findings as artists wrote more about "life and freedom" (societal conditions) and less about "courtship and nightlife" (interpersonal connection) following the upheavals. Cultural upheavals modify individual and collective verbal behavior, demonstrating their far-reaching impact on society.
2609.17225.paper_summary_zh: 文化動盪影響社會生活的許多方面，許多研究已經探討了它們對語言模式的影響。然後，少數調查在流行媒體中大規模孤立了動盪對個體的影響。當前的研究評估了超過一個世紀的數百萬首歌曲歌詞，以尋找越南戰爭、9/11恐怖襲擊和COVID-19所帶來的藝術家內部和藝術家之間的痛苦信號。與五年的基準相比，越南戰爭和9月11日之後，自我參照的比率——一個心理距離的標誌——顯著降低。與動盪前相比，動盪後的認知處理術語有所上升，這表明藝術家們在努力從這些巨大干擾中尋找意義。內容模式證實了這些發現，因為藝術家們在動盪之後寫了更多關於「生活和自由」（社會條件）的內容，而較少提及「戀愛和夜生活」（人際連結）。文化動盪改變了個體和集體的言語行為，顯示出它們對社會的深遠影響。
2609.17225.author: David M. Markowitz et.al.
